passive_examples.sentence: Most product ids are not promoted, and a probe that fails scans all 3,000 elements.
The batch path is already written and already uses array parameters ( CODE ).
CODE allocates one CODE per frame and does one CODE dict lookup per frame, which costs about 50–150 µs after the source files are cached.
CODE — CODE runs one full CODE pass over the template for each parameter, so the template is scanned N times for N parameters.

longest_sentences: Each cell costs about 300–500 ns: one function call, one string comparison, one CODE or one band scan, and three dict operations. 2,000 cells cost 0.6–1.0 ms per search, which is 2% to 3% of the 30 ms search p50.
The page cache normally serves the read, so count about 50 µs for the syscalls and the copy; a cold read costs 23 random 4 KB SSD reads at 20 µs each, which is 460 µs.
The 25 KB also crosses the wire: at 40 req/s that is 1 MB/s of database traffic, and the transfer plus the decode add roughly 0.3–0.5 ms to a query whose round trip is 0.5–2 ms.
At 1,200 req/s that is 840–1,560 ms of CPU time per second, which is more than one full core. p50 is 8 ms, so the parse is 9–16% of p50 before the event loop stall.
Assume a simple indexed query costs 0.5–2 ms, as CODE states. 25 sequential queries cost 25 × 0.5 ms = 12.5 ms at best and 25 × 2 ms = 50 ms at worst.
The gateway therefore loses 17% to 66% of its wall clock to a stall during which every other request queues. p50 is 8 ms, so one 20 ms stall alone is 2.5 times p50.
